title: Metal Ghost Shell — How far can one solo dev push a game using AI?
author: Funny_Bell_3799
selftext:
I’ve been developing **Metal Ghost Shell**, a sci-fi stealth game, as a solo developer and wanted to share where the project has reached.

AI has become a significant part of my production pipeline. I’m using it across character artwork, voice and audio assets, development assistance, prototyping and rapid iteration.

What I've found interesting is that AI hasn't really removed the development work — it's changed **where I spend my time**. Instead of needing a team to produce assets across multiple disciplines, I can spend more of my time designing the game, building and integrating systems, iterating on mechanics and deciding what actually belongs in the finished product.

The video shows the current playable prototype/demo and where that workflow has gotten me so far.

I'm curious how this compares with other solo developers here. **Has AI actually reduced your workload, or has it mostly shifted your workload into direction, selection, integration and refinement?**

For me, that distinction has become much more interesting than simply asking whether AI makes development “faster.”

If anyone wants to try the playable demo as well, gameplay feedback is very welcome.

**Playable demo:** [https://skytalon-ai.itch.io/metal-ghost-shell](https://skytalon-ai.itch.io/metal-ghost-shell)
